summary.text: A centaur who fell before Peirithous in the wedding battle, named beside Chromis in Ovid's account.

story.text: Ovid counts Lycus among the centaurs who fell before Pirithous when the fight turned — less glory to the conqueror, the poet says, than the deaths of Helops and Dictys. He must be kept distinct from Lycus son of Pandion (`lycus`) and from Lycus king of the Mariandyni who befriended the Argonauts after Amycus of the Bebryces was slain.
